argv:
Rewrite the text following Google's developer documentation style.

Write in the second person and the present tense. Use the active voice and
standard American spelling. Keep the tone precise and even-handed rather than
casual — this is documentation, not conversation. Write complete sentences;
do not use fragments for effect, and do not use contractions.

Prefer short sentences and short paragraphs. Use a numbered list for a
sequence of steps and a bulleted list for an unordered set. Begin each list
item with a capital letter.

Avoid the words "simply", "easily", "just", "obviously", and "of course": what
is obvious to the writer is rarely obvious to the reader. Do not use
placeholder words like "please" in instructions. Avoid metaphors, idioms, and
cultural references that will not translate, and avoid asides or personality
that could distract a reader who is scanning for an answer.

Use inclusive, unambiguous language and spell out an abbreviation on first
use. When in doubt, prefer the more explicit and fully spelled-out phrasing
over the more familiar-sounding one.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
It is interesting to contemplate an entangled bank, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singing on the bushes, with various insects flitting about, and with worms crawling through the damp earth, and to reflect that these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, and dependent on each other in so complex a manner, have all been produced by laws acting around us. These laws, taken in the largest sense, being Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance which is almost implied by reproduction; Variability from the indirect and direct action of the external conditions of life, and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high as to lead to a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence to Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms. Thus, from the war of nature, from famine and death, the most exalted object which we are capable of conceiving, namely, the production of the higher animals, directly follows. There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
</passage>

response.text:
Consider an entangled bank covered with many kinds of plants, birds singing in the bushes, various insects flying about, and worms crawling through the damp earth. Each of these organisms has a complex, distinct structure, and each depends on the others in complex ways. Laws acting around us produce all of these forms.

The following laws, understood in the broadest sense, account for this outcome:

* Growth combined with reproduction.
* Inheritance, a near-inevitable result of reproduction.
* Variability, which arises from the direct and indirect effects of external conditions and from use and disuse.
* A rate of increase high enough to cause a struggle for life.

The struggle for life leads to natural selection. Natural selection, in turn, causes divergence of character and the extinction of less-adapted forms. The struggle for existence, including famine and death, produces the most significant outcome we can imagine: the emergence of higher animal life.

This view of life reveals a kind of grandeur. Life's fundamental powers were breathed into a few original forms, or perhaps into just one. As this planet has continued to revolve according to the fixed law of gravity, it has evolved countless forms of extraordinary beauty and complexity from that simple beginning. This evolutionary process continues today.
